info.title: CISCO-BGP-POLICY-ACCOUNTING-MIB MIB API
info.description:
BGP policy based accounting information

⚠️ **IMPORTANT - MIB DATA ACCESS**:
This YANG model exists for SMIv2-to-YANG translation purposes, but MIB data on IOS-XE devices is primarily accessed via **SNMP protocol**, not RESTCONF.

**RESTCONF Limitation**: Many MIB paths may return 404 errors via RESTCONF `/data` endpoints because the device exposes MIB data through SNMP, not the YANG datastore.

**Recommended Access Methods**:
- Use SNMP (v2c/v3) to query MIB data directly
- Use NETCONF `<get>` operations for devices supporting YANG-modeled MIB access
- Check device capabilities: some newer IOS-XE versions may support limited RESTCONF access to specific MIBs

**YANG Model Purpose**: These YANG models define the structure of SNMP MIBs in YANG format for tooling compatibility, but do not guarantee RESTCONF data availability.


**📊 YANG Tree:** [View CISCO-BGP-POLICY-ACCOUNTING-MIB structure](https://jeremycohoe.github.io/cisco-ios-xe-openapi-swagger/yang-trees/CISCO-BGP-POLICY-ACCOUNTING-MIB.html)

get.description: Retrieve cbpAcctTable operational data from MIB

schema.description:
The cbpAcctTable provides statistics about ingress and egress 
        traffic on an interface. This data could be used for purposes 
        like billing.

cbpAcctTrafficIndex.description:
An integer value greater than 0, that uniquely identifies
            a traffic-type. The traffic-type has no intrinsic meaning.
            It just means the traffic coming into an interface can be
            differentiated into different types. It is up to the user to
            give meaning to and configure the various traffic-types on an 
            interface.

cbpAcctInPacketCount.description:
The total number of packets received for a particular
            traffic-type on an interface.

cbpAcctInOctetCount.description:
The total number of octets received for a particular
            traffic-type on an interface.

cbpAcctOutPacketCount.description:
The total number of packets transmitted for a particular
            traffic-type on an interface.

cbpAcctOutOctetCount.description:
The total number of octets transmitted for a particular
            traffic-type on an interface.

parameters.name: Accept
parameters.description: RESTCONF response media type (RFC 8040)

parameters.name: depth
parameters.description: Limit the depth of returned sub-tree data (RFC 8040 Section 4.8.2). Use 'unbounded' for full depth.

parameters.name: fields
parameters.description: Select specific fields to return (RFC 8040 Section 4.8.3). Example: fields=name;status

parameters.name: content
parameters.description: Filter by config state: 'config' (config true only), 'nonconfig' (config false only), or 'all'.
